title: Implement FT-004 operations HTTP routes and integrated evidence
verify: Protected FT-004 routes match Plant Operations HTTP request/response shapes, status codes, no-store behavior, UUID/timestamp/enum handling, and stable error envelope.

API tests prove ActorContext is resolved before business logic and that Boss/Engineer can operate while Consultant, revoked grant, disabled membership, unauthorized Plant, wrong Farm, and archived Plant receive no-leak denials.
Integrated flow proves an Engineer with tomato_001 access creates an observation plus pH/EC check-in and receives a fresh PostgreSQL-derived projection and timeline refs.
Failure-injection tests prove persistence or timeline failures do not return success and do not leak raw exceptions, SQL, credentials, session material, or provider payloads.
FT-004 docs remain synchronized without claiming photo upload, Plant history UI, agents, Safety Gate, action tasks, follow-up, or PWA completion.

constraints: Use the service boundary from TASK-019; do not bypass it from HTTP handlers.
Expose only the FT-004 operations routes; do not accept multipart photo uploads or implement history/timeline presentation.
Return no-leak 404-style Plant denials for missing, unauthorized, revoked, wrong-Farm, or archived normal-operation paths.
Keep response bodies free of credentials, password hashes, session tokens, cookies, headers, raw SQL errors, provider payloads, and hidden reasoning.
invariants: ActorContext must resolve before FT-004 route business logic.
Write routes require active Plant operate authority at the same boundary as persistence.
Latest measurement projection reads PostgreSQL state, not timeline or presentation artifacts.
Timeline refs remain audit/export refs and never become runtime authority.

Trace FT-004-BHV-001 through FT-004-BHV-003 to concrete API/integration tests.
purpose: Expose the completed FT-004 service through protected HTTP routes and prove the end-to-end authorized daily check-in behavior.

No agent output, Safety Gate, action task, follow-up, or PWA implementation.
No feature lifecycle overclaim beyond FT-004 backend operations.
